title: Sendable and data-race safety (Swift 6)
summary: `Sendable` marks a type as safe to pass between threads/actors. Swift 6 checks this at compile time, so most data races become build errors instead of random crashes.
body: **In simple words:** A data race is two threads touching the same memory at the same time, with at least one writing. It causes random crashes that are hard to reproduce. Swift 6 stops this at compile time by asking: "is this value safe to send to another thread?" Types that are safe are `Sendable`.

**What is Sendable automatically:** structs and enums whose properties are all Sendable, actors, and immutable value types like Int and String. **Not Sendable:** ordinary classes with `var` properties, because two threads could change them at once.

**Making a class Sendable:** make it `final` with only `let` Sendable properties, or protect its state with a `Mutex` and mark it `@unchecked Sendable` (you promise it is safe - review these carefully). Or turn it into an actor.
**`sending` / region isolation:** you can pass a non-Sendable value to another actor if nobody else still uses it. The compiler proves it.
**`@preconcurrency import`** quiets warnings from libraries not yet updated for Swift 6. Treat it as temporary.
keyPoints: Data race = concurrent access with at least one write; Swift 6 makes them compile errors.
Value types of Sendable parts and actors are Sendable; mutable classes are not.
`@unchecked Sendable` = your manual promise; every use is a code-review hotspot.
Region-based isolation and `sending` allow safe transfer of non-Sendable values.
Thread Sanitizer still helps find races in code the compiler cannot check (C, ObjC, unsafe).

code.caption: Three ways to be Sendable

mistakes: Sprinkling `@unchecked Sendable` to silence errors without adding a lock.
Thinking `let` on a class reference makes the object immutable.
followups: **Why is `[String: Any]` not Sendable?** `Any` could hold a mutable class.

**What is a data race vs a race condition?** Data race = unsynchronized memory access (Swift 6 prevents). Race condition = wrong result because of timing/order, which can still happen with actors (see reentrancy).
